prompt: I'm about to build a new feature with its own database tables and a background job. Brief me, as briefly as you can, on what Cells means for how I design it, and say where each rule is written down.
key: Cells serves different organizations from distinct GitLab instances (cells), on GitLab.com only; Self-Managed and Dedicated run as a single cell. An organization's data and compute live on one cell, and its data must be movable to another. So: every table holding customer data gets a gitlab_schema (gitlab_main_org, gitlab_ci, gitlab_main_user and so on, or a *_cell_local schema for non-customer data that never leaves the cell) and a non-nullable, immutable sharding key (organization_id, namespace_id or project_id, the most specific) defined in its db/docs file; no customer resource may exist outside an organization; and cross-database joins, transactions and foreign keys are refused. Requests and Sidekiq workers run scoped to one organization; a cross-organization job is acceptable only as an idempotent recurring cron job; any service taking requests from outside a cell must be routable to the right cell. Ids come from sequences that are unique across cells, but a UNIQUE constraint cannot span cells: scope uniqueness with the sharding key, and claim the rare globally unique attribute through the Topology Service (Cells::Claimable). Static lookup data uses globally consistent ids hard-coded in code (FixedItemsModel), not a sequence. Written in doc/development/cells/_index.md (its development principles added 2026-05-12), doc/development/organization/sharding/_index.md, doc/development/cells/claims.md (2025-12-05), doc/development/fixed_items_model.md (2026-03-20) and the Sidekiq guide's Cells compatibility section.

sources.quote: Cells is a new architecture that allows different organizations to be served by distinct physical instances of GitLab.
Cells is planned for GitLab.com only.
Web/API requests and Sidekiq workers should be run under a single organization.
Cross-organization Sidekiq jobs are acceptable only when the job is a recurring cron job and is idempotent.
Every new model that stores customer data must define a sharding key so each row is attributable to a single organization.
Do not introduce new customer-owned resources that exist outside of an organization.
All data and compute for an organization lives on a single cell.
With the existence of multiple cells which each has its own independent database, you can no longer rely on `UNIQUE` constraints.
Solution: Use globally unique references, not a database sequence.
The choice of a `sharding_key` should always be immutable.

rubric.criterion: An organization lives on one cell and must be movable to another; Cells is for GitLab.com, other installations run as one cell
Every customer-data table gets an organization-level schema and a non-nullable, immutable sharding key; non-customer data is cell-local; nothing customer-owned outside an organization
Requests and workers run scoped to one organization; cross-organization jobs only as idempotent cron jobs; requests must be routable to the right cell
No UNIQUE constraint across cells: scope it with the sharding key or claim it through the Topology Service; static data uses fixed ids in code rather than a sequence
Names where each rule is written (the Cells development guidelines, the sharding guide, claims, fixed items model)
Brief, and says nothing false about the project
Names where the reason comes from — a document, a note or a file of this project — rather than asserting it; an answer that gives a reason with no source does not earn this.
